The story of this sequence is often told too simply, so here is what the record shows. Leland Stanford paid for the work. Eadweard Muybridge staged it and patented the method, and the engineer John D. Isaacs later said he designed the camera triggers; who deserved the credit was argued over at the time. The 1878 card names the rider only as "G. Domm," and the photographs show him in silhouette; little else about him is known. A later Muybridge plate, from about 1887, shows a jockey who appears to be Black and whose name was never recorded. Jordan Peele's film *Nope* (2022) imagined that rider's family. And these photographs are not the first animation: drawings were made to move in the 1830s.
